note: Gemini is called only from the server, so there is no ai_browser_call. No .env is committed and no key is in client code, so no secret_exposure. Storage is a GCS bucket with no client access, so no database_rules. The app is anonymous by design, using a session token, so no auth_gap. No tool moves money or sends anything, so there is no ai_tool_unbounded. The main risk is safety logic that the prompts call code-validated (tiers, envelopes, material math), which the model does. The deterministic tools for these exist but are never called. A silent switch to mock mode fabricates plans. Not reviewed: research/, tests/, evidence-deliverables/ (committed sample PDF and xlsx files), the other skills and workflows beyond grep, and index.css. No file was blocked.

labels.what: If the Gemini client fails to start, the code silently sets MOCK_VERTEX_AI=true for the whole process. Every stage then returns canned text and mock extraction, with no error shown to the user.
Regional cost table has one demo ZIP (95120 = 1.55x). Every other ZIP silently gets 1.0, while the app promises cost for the user's ZIP code.
Allergy 'screen' only checks whether an allergen word appears in the product's own name, category or brand. It has no ingredient data, so most real conflicts are stamped allergy_screened=True.

Mock replies tell the user 'No allergy conflicts found', 'Safety permit classifications logged' and 'Task completed successfully' with no model call or check run. They reach real users after the silent fallback.
When the GCS write fails, the session is saved to the container's temp folder and the request still succeeds. On restart or another instance the session is gone.

Mock extraction fabricates the dossier: ZIP 95120, 80 sq ft, allergies [] (confirmed none), a $19k-22k design, 'Mock electrical wiring' as DIY-eligible tier_2 with consent True, $500 tile, can live through it. Runs in production after the silent fallback.
Default scope object starts with allergies=[] (means family confirmed none), budget check 'plausible', a house and owner-occupied. If extraction is skipped or fails, these stand as real answers.
Synthesis phase checklists and budget-gap options are the same fixed strings for every project, shown in the final plan.

Principle 9 says measurement math, quantity and waste, cost lookup and envelope checks run as deterministic tools. Only the scope ballpark and the allergy screen are called. measurement_math, lighting_calc and envelope_check are never called. Design estimates and material costs come from the model via extraction.

Principle 6 says Materials runs a code-level numeric check of each product against the stored safety envelope. envelope_check on each line item is whatever the model wrote; validate_envelope is never called.

Principles 2 and 5 say tiers come from a frozen IRC/NEC matrix (structural trigger at 1,500 lb, panel amps). The tier on each item is taken from the model's own reply by extraction. No code compares items to the matrix, and evaluate_weight_band is unused.

Tier-1 firewall: never give DIY procedure for professional-only work. The chat reply goes to the user after only internal-tag scrubbing. Nothing blocks procedure text, and the DIY filter trusts the model-assigned tier.
Directive says a Tier-2 DIY procedure MUST include permit and inspection hold-points. The merge accepts an empty hold_points list and the DIY gate never checks it.

Prompt says an allowance unit mismatch makes the tool refuse to compute, and allergy handling is code-validated. No unit-match or extended-cost code exists. Quantities, waste and totals are model numbers copied into the xlsx.

Design prompt lists measurement math, IES lighting calc and a refined-estimate cost tool. None is called. Room area, lighting and over_ceiling come from the model, and synthesis uses over_ceiling to decide the budget gap. The 40 ft implausible-size check never runs.
Tier-1 acknowledgement is recorded on every Tier-1 item when any user turn matches a loose regex ('understood', 'hire a contractor'), even if said about something else.
429 message and comment say 1 chat request per minute, and the UI says wait 1 minute. Config default is 10 per minute with burst 5.
Cost bands per sq ft, regional factor, contingency 10-20% and reality thresholds are hardcoded in code and copied as text in the pricing skill prompt.
GCS bucket name defaults to 'reno-compass-checkpoints'. Bucket names are global, so every deploy targets the same name.

Every chat logs the full dossier (allergies, budget, ZIP, contractor quote text) with the session token at DEBUG, to console and a log file. Many other lines log the token. The project's own rule says redact these.

Rate limit is keyed on the client-supplied cookie value, so a new or random cookie gets a fresh bucket. The limiter map never shrinks. /api/session/new and restore-pdf have no limit. Each chat turn makes 2 to 4 paid Gemini calls. /api/chat takes a raw dict payload with no message length cap.

Session token is saved to localStorage (also at lines 32 and 351) and sent in JSON bodies, which defeats the HttpOnly cookie. The token is printed in the chat after a restore (line 354). The cookie has no Secure flag.

Restore-from-PDF trusts the uploaded dossier. Scope and design data are kept (design is not reset), and their free text goes into model prompts as trusted state. Only the contractor quote is fenced. No upload size limit.
Error handlers return raw exception text (str(exc)) to the client. The same happens at lines 963 and 1076 and in the middleware.
System and warning messages use innerHTML with the uploaded file name and server text (line 340), so a crafted file name runs as HTML.
Session token is only checked for the 'reno_s_' prefix, then joined into a file path in local-fallback mode, so '../' can reach JSON files outside the session folder.
Service-account JSON from an env var is written to a temp file with delete=False and never removed.
The raw user message goes into the model prompt next to the trusted dossier state with no guard. The Tier-1 firewall depends on the prompt resisting pressure.

Prompt says implausible measurements (a 40 ft room, a 6 inch ceiling) are flagged and never fed into area math. validate_room_dimensions is never called, and room sizes come straight from model extraction.
Prompt says never ask more than 3 questions in one response. No code checks the reply.
